display.title: Episode 456: The Baal Shem Tov and the Ten Wedding Gifts, Chapter 3 (Yud-Tes Kislev)
display.summary_short: Yud-Tes Kislev, the Alter Rebbe's day of redemption; Shema with a yeshivah boy; and chapter 3 of the Ten Wedding Gifts, as ten strange gifts are announced and a lost child knocks in a blizzard.
display.summary_long: Broadcast two days before Yud-Tes Kislev 5751, in the year of wonders. Uncle Yossi explains that on 19 Kislev 5559 (1798) the Alter Rebbe, Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, was miraculously freed from prison and cleared of all charges, which is why the day is called the Chag HaGeulah. Chassidim retell its stories, divide the whole Talmud so that each person learns a tractate during the year, and make resolutions; every Tzivos Hashem soldier should add to his daily learning. After the Hakochainik march, a ten-year-old yeshivah student recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. In chapter 3 of 'The Baal Shem Tov and the Ten Wedding Gifts', each of the ten students announces a gift to the young couple, every one the property of a local poritz, and the Baal Shem Tov departs in a driverless wagon. Months later, on a night of fierce blizzard, Avraham and Sarah take in a lost, freezing child from the mansion beyond the forest. To be continued. The show ends with the reminder to begin saying 'V'sein tal umatar', a request for letters about Yud-Tes Kislev resolutions, and the year's earliest candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Yud-Tes Kislev is a time to thank Hashem and add in Torah learning; Hashem watches every creature and rewards kindness in His own way.
